name: Green Mountain National Forest
blurb: Northern hardwoods, beech mast, moose and the bears and coyotes that follow them.

tip.title: Take away the beech
tip.text: Beechnuts feed bears, deer and chipmunks in autumn. Set American beech to -100% and watch those animals, then the predators that hunt them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A common hardwood of the northern forest on the lower slopes. Its nuts are an autumn food for bears, deer and small mammals.

nodes.name: Balsam fir
nodes.desc: A conifer of the cooler, higher slopes. Beavers, deer and red squirrels are recorded feeding on it.
A small understory tree whose twigs and leaves are browsed by moose and deer.
A woodland wildflower of the forest floor in cool northern woods. Deer are recorded eating it.
The most recorded large herbivore near the forest. It browses twigs, buds and herbs and eats beechnuts.
A large browser of young hardwood growth. Winter ticks have caused many moose deaths in Vermont in recent years.
Cuts trees to build dams, and the ponds it makes create wetland habitat for many other species.
A slow tree-climbing herbivore that eats bark and leaves of hardwoods and conifers.
A small forest squirrel that feeds on conifer seeds, buds and bark, and is prey for many carnivores.
A ground-dwelling omnivore eating nuts, seeds and some invertebrates, and is prey for foxes, bobcats and coyotes.
A small grazer of clearings and wet meadows that feeds many predators.
A small canid hunting voles and squirrels, and scavenging carrion in winter.
A flexible omnivore that takes small mammals and carrion in the forest edge and near streams.
A large scavenging bird that feeds on carcasses of deer and moose through winter.
The main wild canid predator of the region. It takes small mammals and deer and also scavenges carrion.
A secretive cat that hunts squirrels, voles and hares and sometimes deer in the forest.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore feeding on beechnuts, berries, insects and carrion, and occasionally on calves or fawns.
Drives growth of the canopy and understory plants in the short northern summer.
Leaf litter and rich soils on the slopes hold the nutrients that trees and wildflowers draw on.
Break down leaf litter, dead wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
